lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: A four-game surge has met its first pothole, not a cliff. The Maple Leafs' 5-2 loss to Calgary on Monday snapped that run and left Kirill Marchenko with a lower-body injury - a sharper concern than the standings, where Toronto remains 7-5, third in the Eastern Conference with 16 points, three behind the lead. Jack Roslovic, meanwhile, has become the welcome surprise: six points across the three games before Calgary and a first-line presence beside Auston Matthews, proof that his best hockey may finally have arrived. The harder question sits in the crease. Sergei Bobrovsky is still searching for his footing, and Toronto cannot keep asking its forwards to erase every defensive lapse. One loss does not justify panic, but it demands correction. Tonight's 10 p.m. visit to Seattle is the test: stabilize the goaltending, survive Marchenko's absence and turn a stumble into a response.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season is over, and Toronto's 79-83 finish demands more than cosmetic repairs. The warning arrived yesterday: George Springer was sidelined by lower-back spasms after crashing into the fence - a reminder that this roster's age and durability are now roster-building issues, not footnotes. Vladimir Guerrero Jr. must also rebound from a career-low .688 OPS, making his winter work with his father and uncle the club's most consequential internal project. The rotation is the larger fire: José Berríos may miss 2027 after Tommy John surgery, while Max Scherzer and Shane Bieber reach free agency. Milwaukee's World Series run offers the blueprint - pressure, athleticism, and pitching depth - not another expensive patch. Toronto finished second in the AL East, but the record still says 79-83. Watch the next move: an outfield power bat and at least one dependable starter must arrive before camp, or this rebuild will merely change its stationery.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The early glow has met its first hard reality: Toronto's promising start now runs through a star in street clothes. Kawhi Leonard will miss at least a week with swelling in his left knee after an MRI showed no structural damage, a setback that still carries the familiar weight of Leonard's long injury history. The Raptors are 2-1, third in the Atlantic Division and riding a one-game losing streak after Sunday's 117-94 defeat by Minnesota - their first loss of the season. Scottie Barnes' charge to "hold the fort down" is no slogan; it is the immediate assignment. Toronto must replace Leonard's two-way gravity without pretending one player can duplicate it. Tonight at 7:30 p.m. ET, Orlando visits for the next test - and the Raptors' response will reveal whether this is a stumble or the start of a deeper adjustment.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The bye week did not quiet Washington's crisis; it sharpened it. At 1-4-1, third in the NFC East and riding a one-game losing streak, the Commanders remain 2.5 games back - but "still in contention" now sounds less like confidence than a dare. Terry McLaurin's season-ending knee injury has blown a hole through the offense, and the scrutiny on the front office is deserved. Jayden Daniels threw for 300 yards in the 23-17 loss to San Francisco, yet coach Dan Quinn has backed criticism that the quarterback is playing too cautiously while the new offense sputters. The replacement plan starts with rookie Antonio Williams, who has 18 catches for 205 yards and a touchdown, and should see more targets. Washington gets no softer landing: Sunday night against Philadelphia is the immediate test of whether this team is alive in the NFC East - or merely lingering.

article.title: Raptors Face Magic Without Leonard
paragraphs: The Raptors host the Magic at 7:30 p.m. with Kawhi Leonard out at least a week because of knee swelling. Toronto is 2-1, while Bittle is also out with a foot injury. The Leafs head to Seattle for a 10 p.m. meeting with the Kraken on Sportsnet. Anthony Stolarz is projected to start against Philipp Grubauer, and Marchenko is day-to-day with a lower-body injury. Toronto enters at 7-5, third in the Eastern Conference.

The Jays have no game listed today, but their prospects are in Arizona Fall League action, giving the organization a forward-looking baseball watch. The Commanders, 1-4-1 and third in the NFC East, host the Eagles Sunday at 8:20 p.m. on NBC. Washington is still in contention, but the stakes are high this week. The Raptors-Magic game is at Scotiabank Arena.
